title: Coder Agents Enable Running AI Coding Workflows on Self-Hosted Infrastructure
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/05/coder-agents-self-hosted-ai/en/headerimage/coder-agents-self-hosted-ai-1778516884639.jpeg"/><p>Coder Agents is a model-agnostic platform designed to let organizations run AI coding agents on their own infrastructure, rather than relying on cloud-based services. This allows teams to maintain full control over code, data, and execution environments.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Netflix Serves 84% of Query Results from Cache with Interval-Aware Caching in Apache Druid
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/05/netflix-druid-interval-cache/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1777092326529.jpg"/><p>Netflix improves Apache Druid performance with interval aware caching, serving 84% of analytics results from cache and reducing query load by 33%. The system decomposes rolling window queries into reusable time segments, enabling partial cache reuse and recomputation only for recent data. At scale, it reduces scan volume, improves P90 latency, and optimizes real time analytics workloads.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Presentation: Evolution of a Backend for a Streaming Application
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/streaming-application-aws-infrastructure/en/mediumimage/medium-1778061840987.jpg"/><p>Daniele Frasca explains the architectural evolution of Joyn, a German streaming giant. He discusses moving from fragile single-node setups to resilient serverless architectures using AWS. He shares insights on the Hub and Spoke pattern for data consistency, cell-based isolation to reduce blast radius, and cost-optimization strategies for achieving affordable multi-region active-active setups.</p> <i>By Daniele Frasca</i>

title: Article: Local-First AI Inference: A Cloud Architecture Pattern for Cost-Effective Document Processing
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/local-first-ai-inference-cloud/en/headerimage/Local-First-AI-Inference-A-Cloud-Architecture-Pattern-for-Cost-Effective-Document-Processing-header-1778141518292.jpg"/><p>The Local-First AI Inference pattern routes 70–80% of documents to deterministic local extraction at zero API cost, reserving Azure OpenAI calls for edge cases and flagging low-confidence results for human review. Deployed on 4,700 engineering drawing PDFs, it cut API costs by 75% and processing time by 55%, while bounding errors through a human review tier.</p> <i>By Obinna Iheanachor</i>

title: Podcast: From Java EE to Quarkus and LLMs: Adam Bien’s Playbook for Boring, Future‑Proof Systems
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/podcasts/java-ee-quarkus-llm/en/smallimage/the-infoq-podcast-logo-thumbnail-1777449793047.jpg"/><p>Adam Bien, an independent consultant and pioneer of zero dependencies in the enterprise world of Java, highlights the benefits of consistently using standards, regardless of whether they involve Java or existing patterns. He argues that by doing so, he managed to future-proof the systems he built, preparing them for the cloud era and even for the AI-Native era.</p> <i>By Adam Bien</i>

title: New DORA Report Claims Strong Engineering Foundations Drive AI Return on Investment
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/05/dora-roi-ai-assisted-dev-report/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1778428945703.jpg"/><p>Google Cloud's DORA team released a report detailing a framework for assessing the ROI of AI in software development. It emphasizes that successful AI implementation depends on organizational systems rather than just tools. The report introduces a J-Curve model for value realization. It also discusses the importance of workforce retention and process redesign for achieving long-term gains.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: Netflix Introduces ‘Model Lifecycle Graph’ to Scale Enterprise Machine Learning
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/05/netflix-ml-graph/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1778283879608.jpg"/><p>Netflix has developed a graph-based architecture for managing machine learning systems, called the Model Lifecycle Graph. This system maps interconnections between datasets, models, features, and workflows, addressing challenges in scaling ML operations. It enhances discoverability, governance, and component reuse while supporting a self-service approach for engineers and data scientists.</p> <i>By Matt Foster</i>

title: Java News Roundup: GraalVM, Spring AI, JobRunr, GlassFish, Grails, Groovy, Quarkus Agent MCP
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/05/java-news-roundup-may04-2026/en/headerimage/java-news-roundup-image-1778441049106.jpg"/><p>This week's Java roundup for May 4th, 2026, features news highlighting: OpenJDK JEPs targeted for JDK 27; the sixth milestone release of Spring AI 2.0; the first milestone release of Grails 8.0; the first alpha release of Groovy 6.0; a point release of JobRunr; maintenance releases of GlassFish, TomEE and Tomcat; an accelerated release train for GraalVM; and a new Quarkus Agent MCP server.</p> <i>By Michael Redlich</i>

title: MySQL 9.7: First Major LTS Since 8.4 Brings Enterprise Features to Community Edition
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/05/mysql-97-lts/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1777530966582.jpg"/><p>Oracle has announced the general availability of MySQL 9.7.0, marking the start of a new 9.7 LTS release series and the first major one since MySQL 8.4. The release arrives amid community concerns about declining MySQL development activity and Oracle's long-term commitment to the project.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: Fonttrio Launches as Open-Source Font Pairing Registry for shadcn/ui
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Fonttrio is an open-source font pairing registry designed for shadcn/ui projects, featuring 49 curated font combinations that can be installed via a single command. Developed by Dima Kapish, it streamlines font selection and configuration for web applications. The tool integrates seamlessly with shadcn CLI, generating CSS variables and typography scales automatically.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: Cloudflare Ships Dynamic Workflows, Bringing Durable Execution to Per-Tenant and Per-Agent Code
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/05/cloudflare-dynamic-workflows/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1778146936420.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare released Dynamic Workflows, an MIT-licensed library that extends its durable execution engine so workflow code can differ per tenant, agent, or request at runtime. Built on Dynamic Workers, the library enables platforms to serve millions of unique durable workflows at near-zero idle cost. CI/CD and agent plan execution are the headline use cases.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: AWS Improves Aurora Serverless: 45% Faster Ramp-Up, 30% Higher Throughput
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/05/aurora-serverless-v4/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1777309076897.jpg"/><p>AWS has recently announced that WorkMail will be discontinued and that App Runner will stop accepting new customers and move into maintenance mode. Several other less popular services and features are also entering maintenance or sunset phases, triggering concern and debate across the AWS community.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: How GitHub Is Securing Agentic Workflows in Modern CI CD Systems
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/05/github-agentic-workflows/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1777009566990.jpg"/><p>GitHub detailed a defense-in-depth security architecture for agentic workflows in CI/CD pipelines, focusing on isolation, constrained execution, and auditability. The design aims to safely integrate autonomous AI agents while mitigating risks like prompt injection, privilege escalation, and unintended actions, using sandboxed environments, restricted permissions, and full execution traceability.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Presentation: Leadership in AI-Assisted Engineering
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/ai-assisted-engineering/en/mediumimage/justin-medium-1777371783790.jpg"/><p>Justin Reock discusses the reality of AI’s impact on engineering, moving past anecdotes to hard data from DORA and DX research.  He explains the "GenAI Divide" - where 95% of pilots fail - and shares how leaders can use the SPACE and Core 4 frameworks to measure true ROI.  He explains how to balance speed with quality, reduce developer fear, and apply agentic solutions across the entire SDLC.</p> <i>By Justin Reock</i>

title: Cloudflare Launches “Artifacts” Beta, Introducing Git-Like Versioning for AI Agents
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/05/cloudflare-artifacts-ai-agents/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1777891963459.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has announced the beta release of Artifacts, a new system designed to bring Git-style version control to AI agents, enabling developers to track, manage, and evolve agent-generated outputs with the same rigor as traditional code.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>
